domain: Property purchase tax by autonomous community. Rates are ceded to the regions and change often.
critical_notes: Most reduced rates require the property to be the buyer's vivienda habitual. A non-resident buying a second or holiday home almost never qualifies. A calculator that offers reduced rates by default will understate the tax badly for exactly our audience.
Banded regimes are progressive by tranche, each slice taxed at its own rate. Flattening a banded scale to one number is a real source of error.
Since 1 January 2022 the taxable base is the higher of the agreed price and the Catastro valor de referencia. See minimum_base below.

minimum_base.statement: The taxable base for ITP and AJD on immovable property is the valor de referencia published by the Direccion General del Catastro, or the declared price or consideration where that is higher. The base is the greater of the two.

source.name: BOE consolidated text
source.ref: art. 10 RDLeg 1/1993, as amended by Ley 11/2021 with effect 1 January 2022

minimum_base.tool_design: A calculator cannot compute the valor de referencia; it is property-specific. Compute tax on the entered price, state plainly that this is a MINIMUM, and prompt the user to look up the reference value and re-run if it is higher. Never present the price-based figure as the final number.

foreign_buyer_surcharge.statement: No surcharge on non-resident or foreign buyers is enacted anywhere in Spain.

source.name: Ministerio de Hacienda
source.ref: Tributacion Autonomica 2026, chapters I and II

foreign_buyer_surcharge.notes: The reported state-level tax on non-EU non-resident buyers remains a proposal with no enacting instrument found on BOE. Catalonia's 20 percent rate is a large-holder and whole-building rule that applies equally to Spanish buyers; it is not a nationality rule. The proposed 100 percent charge on non-EU buyers is frequently described as though it were in force. It is not.
